answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the gale ordering is published with the falcon batch, the sparrow audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 49% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 24 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
